newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis says mark-franc parity must be kept - paper.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis says mark-franc parity must be kept - paper.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said in a newspaper interview that the parity between the French franc and the German mark must be maintained, but he reiterated that the U.S. dollar had room to appreciate.
"The parity between the franc and the mark must be maintained at its current level," Arthuis said in an interview in Monday's Les Echos. An advance copy was sent to Reuters.
He said 10-year bond rates in France and Germany of 5.58 percent and 5.62 percent, respectively, provided a basis for his conviction.
Arthuis said he was stunned by former French president Valery Giscard d'Estaing's recent questioning of the franc-mark parity and proposal for a rate of seven francs to the euro.

He reiterated that a rate of seven francs to the euro would hurt French savers. The franc is currently worth around 6.5 ecu's. Ecu's will be exchanged for euros on a one-for-one basis when European monetary union is established in 1999.
"If we take up M. Giscard d'Estaing's proposals, they (savers) would pay seven francs for a euro, when they could have one today for 6.5 francs," Arthuis said.
"As to the parity between the dollar and the franc, I have always said that there was margin for appreciation for the dollar," he said.

He said the best way to drive up the dollar was "collectively, through a single currency -- thus the urgency for the euro and for the convergence of our policies on the basis of stable parities at the heart of the European Union."
He also said joint action should be taken within the framework of the Group of Seven industrial powers and not through "individual initiatives."
Asked about complaints of French industrialists that the franc is overvalued, Arthuis said, "France's competitiveness seems good to me. The trade surplus will undoubtedly reach a new record in 1996."

Arthuis reiterated that the Italian lira's recent return to Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM) was "good news. The circle of stability in Europe is enlarged for the first time to 12 national currencies."
